# Admin | Purchase Lark paid plans

6 min read

I. Intro​

​

🔖

Who can perform these steps: Primary administrators or administrators with "Billing" permission.​

​

Lark offers Starter, Basic, Pro, and Enterprise plans. The Lark Starter plan is activated automatically for newly created organizations at no cost. Other plans need to be purchased. As an administrator, you can purchase a new Basic or Pro plan or additional seats for the Basic, Pro, and Enterprise plans. You can also renew Pro and Enterprise plans in advance.​

  * Organizations on a Starter, Basic (trial), Pro (trial), or Enterprise (trial) plan can purchase a new Basic or Pro plan.​

  * Organizations already on a Basic, Pro, or Enterprise plan can purchase additional seats for their respective plan, but not seats for other plans.​

  * Organizations on a Basic, Pro, or Enterprise plan can renew their subscription in the Lark Admin Console from the subscription's effective date through 30 days after the expiration date.​

# API Explorer Guide

Last updated on 2024-02-08

# API Explorer Guide

# Overview

API Explorer is a tool that can assist you in debugging, testing and using Lark Open APIs.

Through API Explorer, you can easily complete the interface call without writing codes. In addition, we provide the following functions to improve your interface debugging efficiency:

  * Automatically obtain authentication credentials: Bind your application to obtain the token with one click, no additional request needed
  * Built-in scope application: The scopes required for API are clearly stated, apply easily within the tool
  * Sample code to help development: We provide multi-language sample codes, copy and quickly reuse it into your codes

# Try it here

You can enter API Explorer through the developer document by clicking "Try it" next to the description. Also, you can access it through here.

Image

# Components

## Choose your app

The first time you use API Explorer, you need to log in first. For example, the app can obtain the information of a user in Contacts. Obtain the tenant access token
  * user_access_token: A user access token, which allows an app to perform a specific operation on behalf of a user. For example, the app can create Docs or an event via an API. Obtain the user access token

When your app calls an API, it needs to contain an access token in the request `Header` and use the syntax `Authorization:Bearer <access token>`. Different APIs can support one or more types of access tokens.

Using API Explorer, you can obtain the authentication credentials required by the interface automatically without additionally calling the "Get Tenant/User Access Credentials" interface. The obtained token will then be automatically filled in the interface request parameters.

Image

Access token is valid for 7200s, you need to refresh if expired

## Run

### Fill in query parameters

You can fill in the request header, request body, and query parameters, modify the default values of each input parameter to initiate a call, and explore the API response under different input parameters.

# General parameters

Last updated on 2023-11-10

# General parameters

To meet diverse application scenarios, Lark Open Platform provides a rich set of APIs and events for developers to call or subscribe to. These APIs and events involve some general parameters, which are introduced here in a unified manner.

General parameters can be used as request parameters or response parameters. Before using the APIs and events provided by the Lark Open Platform, it is recommended to first understand the meanings of these general parameters.

## App-related parameters

### app_id

`app_id` is the unique identifier of Lark Open Platform app. It is automatically generated by the system when the app is created and cannot be modified by users. You can check the `app_id` in the Credentials & Basic info page of the Developer Console.Image

### app_secret

`app_secret` is the secret key of the app. It is automatically generated by the system when creating an app and is required as one of the request parameters when calling certain APIs. 
  * If data association between different apps is not required, `open_id` can be used.
  * If data association between apps is needed, and the developers belong to the same organization, `union_id` can be used.
  * If data associationbetween apps is needed, and the apps may be developed by different organizations, but the users of the apps belong to the same organization, `user_id` is the appropriate choice.

## Access tokens related parameters

To enhance API call security, Lark Open Platform has implemented an access token mechanism. Before invoking an API, an app must obtain the necessary access credentials, also call `access_token`.

`access_token` represents the authorization granted to an app by the platform, tenant (organization or team), or user. There are three types of access tokens:

  * App access token, with the parameter name `app_access_token`.
  * Tenant access token, with the parameter name `tenant_access_token`.
  * User access token, with the parameter name `user_access_token`.

To learn how to get access tokens, see Get access token.

# Apply for API permissions

Through this article, you can learn what API permissions are and how to apply for them.

## What are API permissions

During app development, you may need to call server APIs of the open platform services, or listen to subscribed events, etc. These operations may require access to tenant and user privacy information or involve manipulation of tenant and user app data. For security reasons, you need to apply for the corresponding permissions for your app. The permissions will take effect only after the app review is approved, and subsequently the app can invoke server APIs or listen to subscribed event list. In simple terms, the API permissions (Scope) of an app determine which server-side capabilities the app can use.

### Permission levels

There are different permission levels for different app types: store apps and custom apps. You can refer to the table below.
